dimensions
dimensions · 5 records
  1. dimension
    demand_forecasting
    assessment
    Consistently conservative quarterly ranges with strong delivery. Long-horizon precision is not established.
    confidence
    High for measured quarterly outcomes; medium for interpretation.
    evidence
    evidence · 2 records
    1. date
      2023Q3–2026Q2
      outcome

    2. date
      2026-06-30
      outcome
      AWS commitments were 496 bn, with a 6.4-year weighted-average remaining term and usage/performance conditions.

      source ids · 1 records

    counterexamples or limits
    counterexamples or limits · 2 records
    1. Above-range results can reflect deliberate conservatism, not uniquely superior demand estimates.
    2. Investment-linked customer financing complicates interpretation of backlog.
    leadership attribution
    Jassy and the finance team own consolidated guidance. Garman became AWS CEO inJune 2024; earlier observations cannot be credited to his CEO tenure.
    valuation use
    Apply to specific scenario conditions; no numeric credibility multiplier.

accounting model requirements
accounting model requirements · 6 records
  1. Forecast physical capex, depreciation, lease additions/payments, inventory and working capital separately in early years; revenue-change/sales-capital is a compressed proxy.
  2. Keep SBC in operating costs; do not add it back without an explicit offset for equity issued to employees.
  3. Separate cash-flow tax benefits of accelerated depreciation from normalized accrual tax; no terminal tax holiday.
  4. Do not capitalize unrealized equity gains or energy derivative gains as operating earnings.
  5. Satisfy terminal identity: terminal sales/capital = ROIC / after-tax operating margin.
  6. Uncommenced leases and purchase commitments are not automatically additional net debt if already included in cash-flow forecasts.
unresolved gaps
unresolved gaps · 3 records
  1. No refreshed October17 balance sheet; use June30 anchor or explicitly bridge subsequently disclosed financing/investment events.
  2. No independent fair-value appraisal of private equity, customer-credit exposures, pending acquisitions or derivatives.
  3. No credible terminal customer-concentration or AI pricing dataset; scenario stresses remain wide.
invalidation checks
invalidation checks · 5 records
  1. AWS growth below 20% for two ordinary quarters despite delivered capacity, or deterioration in customer credit and committed utilization.
  2. Cash capex remains near/above 220 bn without accelerated revenue and operating cash flow in 2027–2028.
  3. Retail margin improvement reverses after tariff-refund normalization or advertising monetization weakens.
  4. Shorter server lives or higher memory and energy costs undermine payback economics.
  5. Material financing, dilution or acquisition cash outflow without matched incremental cash generation.

bounded Model Gaps
bounded Model Gaps · 9 records
  1. Valuation-date stub and post-anchor cash/claims/share roll-forward not integrated; this is a forecast-origin operating EV, not October 17 equity value.
  2. No probability weighting or share-price calibration. Source forecast assumptions are judgments, not reported facts.
  3. Enterprise-to-equity bridge is not computed here; consult the company-specific claim register for resolved evidence, assumptions and remaining uncertainties. Zero is not evidence of absence.
  4. Integrate EBIT with D&A when moving beyond this held-EBIT capital sensitivity.
  5. Cash tax benefit and net interest are budget assumptions; solve with actual funding/tax schedule.
  6. Award cash-settlement budget1bn/year is an explicit0–2bn sensitivity, not verified actual.
  7. Corporate principal refinancing, strategic funding and contingent M&A remain separate cash-use rows; never subtract forecast deficits as debt.
  8. Review financed-facility additions0–3bn/year if incremental to cash capex, with matched financing.
  9. Legacy end-of-explicit capital convention is retained transparently; terminal FCFF growth differs slightly from stable revenue growth. Later gross-capital components are unmodeled, not zero.

convention
Preferred cash-capex forecast excludes capital-creditors movement from operating WC. Track accrued asset additions and capital-creditor balances separately for capacity and paydown stress. If supplier credit is instead debtlike, include accrued capex, show equal financing inflow, and apply one consistent opening-liability claim. Never add 29,267 to cash capex as an unfinanced current cash requirement.

normalization basis
normalization basis · 9 fields
reported asset lives
Buildings up to 40 years; servers/networking 5–6 years; heavy equipment 10–13; other equipment 3–10. Subset server life reduced 6 to5 effective2025; increased2025 D&A by~1,400.
reported PPE cohorts
FY2025 gross server/networking172,492; construction-in-progress71,745; netPPE357,025. June2026 netPPE446,046. TTM PPE D&A49,741 and Q2 annualized55,476.

analyst DA year3 range USDm
analyst DA year3 range USDm · 2 records
  1. 115000
  2. 130000
reasoning
Existing assets plus recent buildout moving in service drive depreciation catch-up. Do not depreciate all new construction from day1 or keep D&A flat as capex surges. As a rough cohort check, 60% server additions over5.5years,30% facilities over25years,10% other over10years gives~13.1% annual depreciation on in-service additions; half-year convention and retirement/CIP schedules can support~65bn next-year D&A. Mix, lives and placement dates are analyst assumptions, not disclosed future mix.
management cycle statement
Management described data-center spending about2years before monetization, servers purchased months before use, server breakeven under3years and longer-lived facilities. This supports an eventual normalization scenario, not certainty of utilization or returns.
non PPE reinvestment basis
Historical combined non-PPE amortization plus tax-adjusted operating-asset/liability cash movements was a 3.9bn source; forecast0–15bn year1 uses to allow Cloud receivables, inventory/content and lease-payment timing, excluding capital creditors and financing investments.
years after7
Fade temporary implied capital productivity toward existing terminal S:C0.98684, consistent with12%ROIC / (16%margin ×76%after-tax share). No lower terminal reinvestment/free-cash-flow windfall.

valuation and funding policy
valuation and funding policy · 8 records
  1. Discount operating FCFF to obtain operating enterprise value; negative FCFF already reduces EV. Never deduct the cumulative modeled deficit again as current debt.
  2. Present current operating EV independently of cash, debt, finance leases, financing obligations, nonoperating investments and other claim adjustments.
  3. Cash funding bridge adds SBC as a noncash financing source only; its compensation cost remains in valuation FCFF. Do not then impose a second full future SBC value charge. Existing awards/share-count policy remains separate.
  4. Explicit finance-lease asset additions reduce economic FCFF; equal noncash financing supports the liquidity bridge. Principal payments consume cash but are not another operating FCFF deduction.
  5. Keep operating leases as rent in EBIT/OCF unless all EBIT, D&A, capital, capex and debt treatment are recast. Do not subtract96,320 operating lease debt without that recast.
  6. New build-to-suit financing-obligation asset additions not separately disclosed must be checked against the PPE roll-forward. Add a0–3bn/year economic FCFF sensitivity only if incremental to reported cash capex; equal noncash financing offsets liquidity. Do not infer asset additions directly from liability changes.
  7. Capital-creditors timing, accelerated depreciation and customer investment funding are separate mechanisms. Do not call private equity marks deployable cash or treat backlog as funded orders.
  8. An external-funding need is a conditional financing plan: test debt capacity, dilution, covenant/liquidity buffers and cash interest. It does not automatically invalidate operating EV, imply equity issuance, or create an extra debt deduction.
implementation recommendation
Recommend central_normalization as the researched base capital override for years1–7, rather than the initial S:C schedule; review before production. Implement explicit first5–7year cash capex, PPE depreciation, finance-lease additions and non-PPE operating reinvestment schedules. Keep current high-investment S:C path as a sensitivity, not binding disclosed funding. Add a separate cash runway/financing panel, preserve normalized-tax economic FCFF and temporary cash tax benefits, and reconcile the missing financing obligations. No production files changed.

economic formula
NOPAT - (gross cash capex - asset-sale proceeds/incentives + finance-lease additions - PPE D&A + non-PPE operating reinvestment)
cash formula
economic FCFF + gross SBC - award cash settlements + cash-tax benefit + noncash finance-lease funding - net cash interest - lease/financing-obligation principal
later normalization
Years8–15 linearly fade year7 implied incremental S:C to original terminal0.98684; retain original revenue/EBIT/tax/WACC/terminal growth/ROIC.
residual gates
residual gates · 5 records
  1. Integrate EBIT with D&A when moving beyond this held-EBIT capital sensitivity.
  2. Cash tax benefit and net interest are budget assumptions; solve with actual funding/tax schedule.
  3. Award cash-settlement budget1bn/year is an explicit0–2bn sensitivity, not verified actual.
  4. Corporate principal refinancing, strategic funding and contingent M&A remain separate cash-use rows; never subtract forecast deficits as debt.
  5. Review financed-facility additions0–3bn/year if incremental to cash capex, with matched financing.

rationale
rationale · 10 fields
growth
14% sits between FY2025 growth of 12.4% and Q2 2026 growth of 20%. AWS and advertising support expansion, but they cannot justify applying their segment growth to all retail revenue.
target Margin
15% improves on 12.1% TTM as AWS/advertising mix and retail efficiency rise. It remains far below AWS segment margins because consolidated sales include substantial low-margin commerce.
tax
24% is a normalized operating-tax assumption. Recent investment gains distort pretax income and the accounting effective rate, so those gains do not set operating cash tax.
sales Capital
0.8x requires $1.25 of net reinvestment per incremental $1 of sales. AI data centers, fulfillment and working capital keep reinvestment high even with supplier financing; early modeled FCFF can be negative.
terminal ROIC
10% assumes mature capital earns approximately the cost of capital. Scale advantages are largely competed away after the explicit growth period.
wacc
10.0% nominal USD is a rounded model estimate. Assumed beta 1.2, 10% target debt and a 1-point debt spread balance resilient diversified businesses against discretionary spending and the infrastructure funding cycle.
terminal Growth
2.5% nominal USD is a mature-state assumption with limited real expansion, well below the high-growth starting rate and the discount rate; it is not a company forecast.
years
10 years is the common model horizon so company economics can be compared; rates and margins fade over this period. The number is a modeling convention, not a source fact.
other Claims
0 is an unreviewed placeholder, not evidence that no additional claims exist. Review operating/finance leases, financing obligations and minority investments. Current cash is not a complete appraisal of all non-operating assets.
other Assets
0 is an unreviewed placeholder, not a statement that all non-operating assets are absent or worthless. Review assets not already included in snapshot cash and avoid double counting.
